Background Prospective longitudinal follow‐up of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) trajectories after acute cardiac decompensation of heart failure is lacking. We investigated changes in LVEF and covariates at 6‐months' follow‐up in patients with a predischarge LVEF ≤40%, and determined predictors and prognostic implications of LVEF changes through 18‐months' follow‐up. Methods and Results Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure program participants (n=633) were categorized into subgroups based on LVEF at 6‐months' follow‐up: normalized LVEF (>50%; heart failure with normalized ejection fraction, n=147); midrange LVEF (41%–50%; heart failure with midrange ejection fraction, n=195), or persistently reduced LVEF (≤40%; heart failure with persistently reduced LVEF , n=291). All received guideline‐directed medical therapies. At 6‐months' follow‐up, compared with patients with heart failure with persistently reduced LVEF, heart failure with normalized LVEF or heart failure with midrange LVEF subgroups showed greater reductions in LV end‐diastolic/end‐systolic diameters (both P <0.001), and left atrial systolic diameter ( P =0.002), more increased septal/posterior end‐diastolic wall‐thickness (both P <0.001), and significantly greater improvement in diastolic function, biomarkers, symptoms, and health status. Heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, and baseline LVEF were independent predictors of LVEF improvement. Mortality and event‐free survival rates were lower in patients with heart failure with normalized LVEF ( P =0.002). Overall, LVEF increased further at 18‐months' follow‐up ( P <0.001), while LV end‐diastolic diameter decreased ( P =0.048). However, LVEF worsened ( P =0.002) and LV end‐diastolic diameter increased ( P =0.047) in patients with heart failure with normalized LVEF hospitalized between 6‐months' follow‐up and 18‐months' follow‐up. Conclusions Six‐month survivors of acute cardiac decompensation for systolic heart failure showed variable LVEF trajectories, with >50% showing improvements by ≥1 LVEF category. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, suggesting multilevel reverse remodeling, were predictable from several baseline characteristics, and were associated with clinical outcomes at 18‐months' follow‐up. Repeat hospitalizations were associated with attenuation of reverse remodeling. Nonstandard Abbreviations and Acronyms A late atrial filling velocity ACD acute cardiac decompensation E left ventricular early diastolic filling velocity e’ peak early annular velocity FUP18 18‐month follow‐up FUP6 6‐month follow‐up GDMT guideline‐directed medical therapies HFnEF heart failure with normalized ejection fraction INH Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure MR‐proANP midregional pro‐atrial natriuretic peptide sTVG peak systolic tricuspid valve gradient Clinical Perspective What Is New? A relevant proportion of patients diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction after an episode of acute cardiac decompensation, including 41% of those with severely depressed ejection fraction (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] <30%), experienced significant improvements in LVEF within the following 6 months. The majority of patients showed variable LVEF trajectories after acute cardiac decompensation and transitioned between currently defined LVEF‐based heart failure categories; serial long‐term LVEF assessment showed an association between disease progression (based on rehospitalization) and worsening LVEF as a surrogate of reversal/attenuation of reverse remodeling. What Are the Clinical Implications? Because of its association with other remodeling parameters, LVEF (and especially LVEF trajectory) is a useful surrogate marker for risk stratification and outcome prediction following discharge from the hospital after acute cardiac decompensation. Normalization of LVEF may not indicate true disease recovery, highlighting the need for ongoing heart failure therapy. Given the changes in LVEF over time, making therapeutic decisions based on a single LVEF measurement after acute cardiac decompensation seems inappropriate; individual LVEF trajectories during disease progression need to be considered in heart failure phenotyping to facilitate personalized care approaches. Repeat episodes of acute cardiac decompensation (ACD) occur throughout the heart failure (HF) trajectory. ACD is associated with injury and dysfunction of the heart and other organ systems, and patients with ACD frequently require hospitalization. 1 Clinical and functional recovery after ACD is often incomplete; abnormal loading conditions and augmented wall stress may induce adverse changes at the cellular and anatomic level, enhance disease progression, and increase the risk for adverse clinical outcomes. Although originally described after experimental myocardial infarction, 2 left ventricular (LV) remodeling involving alterations in cardiac architecture and systolic and diastolic myocardial dysfunction may also develop in response to other types of myocardial injury. 3 Knowledge that activation of the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone axis and the adrenergic nervous system is implicated in this process drove clinical trials investigating the effects of neurohormonal inhibition on mechanisms of ventricular remodeling and patient outcomes. Early studies including patients with HF with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (HFrEF) showed, for example, that the angiotensin‐converting enzyme inhibitor enalapril prevented progressive left ventricular (LV) dilatation and systolic dysfunction. 4 Subsequent evidence demonstrated that other medications used as part of guideline‐directed medical therapies (GDMT, eg, β‐blockers or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists) are also capable of attenuating or reversing remodeling and improve LV ejection fraction (LVEF), and that there are positive correlations between the effects of an intervention on LV volumes and function and its effect on mortality. 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 Improved LVEF is, in principle, considered a poor surrogate of contractility because of its dependence on LV volumes and loading conditions. 9 However, evidence from observational studies suggests that patients with improvement or even normalization of previously impaired LVEF represent a different clinical entity from those with persistently reduced or preserved LVEF. 8 , 10 , 11 Prospective longitudinal studies on the course of LVEF and other cardiac function and morphology parameters from a clearly defined time point during the HF trajectory are currently lacking, and there is no information on predictors of these changes, associated biomarker trends, and prognostic implications in the setting of ACD. This prospective study investigated patients hospitalized for ACD with a predischarge LVEF of ≤40%, who received GDMT as tolerated throughout follow‐up. Aims of the study were (1) to examine the spectrum of changes in LVEF and other parameters of cardiac function and morphology between baseline assessment before hospital discharge and at 6‐month follow‐up (FUP6) using quantitative echocardiography; (2) to evaluate associated changes in patient characteristics, including symptoms, health status, and biomarkers of myocyte stress and injury, and inflammation; (3) to identify baseline parameters that predict changes in LVEF at FUP6 and assess their impact on the risk of mortality and rehospitalization between FUP6 and 18‐months' follow‐up (FUP18); and (4) to describe longer‐term LVEF trajectories in FUP18 survivors. METHODS The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. Study Design and Patient Sample The investigator‐initiated Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure (INH) program (ISRCTN 23325295) studies the effects of nurse‐coordinated disease management (HeartNetCare‐HF) compared with usual care on all‐cause mortality and morbidity after hospitalization for ACD. Study design and primary results in the first 715 participants were reported previously. 12 In brief, patients were eligible if aged ≥18 years and hospitalized for ACD (dyspnea at rest plus at least 1 of the following: raised jugular venous pressure, peripheral edema, or pulmonary congestion [clinical or chest radiography]). Patients from 9 sites in lower Franconia or Baden‐Wuerttemberg, Germany, with a LVEF ≤40% measured before discharge were randomly assigned 1:1 to either HeartNetCare‐HF or usual care. The only exclusion criteria were new‐onset structural heart disease (eg, type 1 myocardial infarction), lack of written informed consent, or logistic or health reasons precluding participation in a telephone‐based intervention. The trial was conducted according to Good Clinical Practice guidelines and Declaration of Helsinki 2002 principles, and was approved by all responsible ethics committees. This substudy included all INH participants who attended the FUP6 visit in person and had 2‐dimensional echocardiograms whose quality allowed for unambiguous determination of LVEF at baseline and FUP6. Patients were divided in subgroups based on their LVEF at FUP6: those with LVEF >50% were categorized as having normalized LVEF (HFnEF); those with LVEF between 41% and 50% as having HF with midrange LVEF (HFmrEF); and those with LVEF ≤40% as having HFrEF. Uptitration of GDMT to target doses was part of the INH study protocol. 12 Baseline Examination and Follow‐Up Patients underwent physical examination, laboratory assessment, ECG, echocardiography, and psychometric evaluation using the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire 13 at baseline and follow‐up visits that took place every 6 months. Follow‐up was centralized and occurred either at the INH outpatient clinic or by structured telephone‐based interview. Information on vital status and hospital admissions was obtained from patients, hospital discharge letters, and medical files, and adjudicated by INH team members blinded to study intervention according to prespecified criteria. For deceased patients, date and cause of death were ascertained using death certificates. “Hospitalization” was defined as unplanned hospital admission with at least 1 overnight stay. Echocardiography Echocardiography was performed as part of routine care using a prespecified protocol based on American Society of Echocardiography recommendations. 14 Two‐dimensional parasternal long‐ and short‐axis views and apical views were recorded. LVEF was determined using Simpson's biplane or monoplane method, and LV end‐diastolic dimensions (LVEDD) and LV end‐systolic dimensions, wall thickness, and left atrial end‐systolic diameter measured from left parasternal M‐mode echocardiograms. LV diastolic function was examined where feasible. LV early diastolic filling velocity (E), late atrial filling velocity (A), E‐wave deceleration time, and the E/A ratio were determined by pulsed‐wave Doppler using the apical 4‐chamber view. Peak early diastolic annular velocity (e') was derived from the pulsed‐wave tissue‐Doppler signal at the lateral mitral annulus. Systolic pulmonary artery pressure was estimated from the peak systolic tricuspid valve gradient (sTVG) using continuous‐wave Doppler.

extracted_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal study investigated Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) trajectories, associated echocardiographic and systemic changes, predictors, and prognostic implications over 18 months in heart failure patients with predischarge LVEF <=40% after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD). The study found variable LVEF trajectories, with over 50% showing improvements by at least one LVEF category within 6 months, indicating multilevel reverse remodeling. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, were predictable from baseline characteristics (e.g., heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, baseline LVEF, lower natriuretic peptide levels), and were associated with improved clinical outcomes (lower mortality and rehospitalization rates) at 18 months. However, repeat hospitalizations were linked to the attenuation or reversal of this reverse remodeling. Biomarkers such as NT-proBNP, MR-proANP, cardiac troponin I, hs-CRP, and interleukin-6 showed significant changes, often decreasing with LVEF improvement, while others like hemoglobin, leukocytes, and renal/hepatic function parameters showed no differential changes across LVEF recovery subgroups.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT) for Heart Failure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMT) as tolerated throughout the 18-month follow-up, with uptitration to target doses as per the Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure (INH) study protocol. The study focused on observing LVEF trajectories and biomarker changes in response to ongoing GDMT rather than comparing specific therapeutic interventions or doses. No explicit dose-response comparisons for individual GDMT components were reported, but proportions of patients taking each substance class were high and increased at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Declined markedly at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline; significantly lower in patients with improved LVEF (HFnEF and HFmrEF) versus those with persistent HFrEF. Overall, levels did not change significantly at 18-month follow-up (FUP18), but decreased significantly between FUP6 and FUP18 only in patients with HFrEF (P=0.006). FUP6 levels were associated with readmissions between FUP6 and FUP18 (odds ratio per 2-fold change, 2.6 [1.9–3.4]; P <0.001); FUP18 levels were higher in HFnEF patients with versus without readmission (mean adjusted ratio 1.20 [1.00–1.43]; P =0.047).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Myocyte stress marker and natriuretic peptide, involved in cardiovascular homeostasis, volume regulation, and indicating cardiac stretch/volume overload.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Recovery from Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) with LVEF improvement, managed with Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), evaluated over 6 and 18 months.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates reduced myocyte stress and injury, associated with improved cardiac function and multilevel reverse remodeling. Lower levels are linked to better clinical outcomes and predict fewer readmissions. Declining levels in HFrEF specifically suggest reverse remodeling, while higher levels at FUP18 in HFnEF patients with readmission suggest renewed stress.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Declined markedly at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline. Lower baseline levels were identified as a significant predictor for LVEF improvement (P<0.05). At FUP6, levels were significantly lower in patients with improved LVEF versus those with persistent HFrEF; HFrEF patients had NT-proBNP levels twice as high as HFmrEF and HFnEF subgroups. Abnormal, albeit lower, levels were still observed in HFnEF at FUP6 despite apparent normalization of LV systolic function.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Natriuretic peptide and biomarker of cardiac wall stress and heart failure severity, associated with cardiac function and neurohormonal activation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) measurements in heart failure patients after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), particularly in relation to LVEF improvement and as a predictor for clinical outcomes.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower baseline levels predict a higher likelihood of LVEF improvement. Persistent abnormal levels at FUP6, even with improved LVEF, suggest ongoing myocardial stress and serve as a predictor for clinical outcomes and renal dysfunction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Declined markedly at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline. Baseline levels were similarly elevated in all heart failure subgroups and declined comparably, resulting in no significant difference between subgroups (LVEF improvement vs. no LVEF improvement) at FUP6.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An acute-phase reactant and a general marker of systemic inflammation and tissue injury response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) measurements in heart failure patients after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), comparing LVEF recovery subgroups.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation. Its comparable decline across LVEF subgroups suggests a general inflammatory response rather than a differential indicator for LVEF recovery, though prolonged or intense inflammation is linked to adverse LV remodeling.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Declined markedly at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline; levels declined significantly more in patients who showed improved LVEF. Initially, it was noted that no significant difference existed between subgroups at FUP6, but further detail clarified a greater decline in the improved LVEF group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in immune response and inflammation, related to adverse left ventricular (LV) remodeling when augmented.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) measurements in heart failure patients after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), comparing LVEF improvement subgroups.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A greater decline in levels is associated with improved LVEF, suggesting beneficial modulation of inflammation and potential for reverse LV remodeling. Increased intensity or duration of inflammation is generally related to adverse LV remodeling.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Declined markedly at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline. Levels were significantly lower in patients with improved LVEF versus patients with persistent HFrEF. HFrEF patients had significantly higher average cardiac troponin I both at baseline and FUP6. A substantial proportion of patients, including those with improved LVEF (HFnEF), still had abnormal (elevated) levels at FUP6, albeit comparatively lower than HFrEF.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A protein component of heart muscle, released into the blood during myocardial injury or damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) measurements in heart failure patients after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), specifically examining differences between LVEF recovery subgroups and in the context of persistent hemodynamic congestion.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Persistent abnormal or elevated levels at FUP6, especially higher levels in HFrEF, suggest ongoing myocardial injury and stress, even with improved LVEF in some cases. Elevated levels can indicate reduced hemodynamic reserve contributing to clinical worsening.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes in hemoglobin levels between baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) did not differ significantly between heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, and HFrEF).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Changes between baseline and FUP6 in various heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, HFrEF) after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant differential change or impact on health status or LVEF recovery was observed between LVEF recovery subgroups in this study, suggesting it is not a key differential indicator in this context.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes in leukocyte levels between baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) did not differ significantly between heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, and HFrEF).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: White blood cells involved in the immune system, defending the body against infection.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Changes between baseline and FUP6 in various heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, HFrEF) after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant differential change or impact on health status or LVEF recovery was observed between LVEF recovery subgroups in this study, suggesting it is not a key differential indicator in this context.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes in renal function parameters did not differ significantly between heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, and HFrEF) at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Patients after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) receiving Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), evaluated at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant differential impact on health status or LVEF recovery was observed between LVEF recovery subgroups in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes in hepatic function parameters did not differ significantly between heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, and HFrEF) at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Liver metabolism, detoxification, and protein synthesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Patients after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) receiving Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), evaluated at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant differential impact on health status or LVEF recovery was observed between LVEF recovery subgroups in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant LVEF improvement occurred within 6 months in the majority of patients (over 50% showed improvement by at least one LVEF category); nearly one quarter experienced normalization to >50%. Greater LV improvements, often >=10%, were observed over time. LVEF also showed additional increases over 12 months in HFmrEF and HFrEF groups. However, LVEF worsened (P=0.002) in patients with normalized LVEF who were rehospitalized between 6 and 18 months.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the pumping efficiency of the left ventricle, indicating systolic cardiac function and ventricular remodeling (both reverse remodeling and its attenuation/reversal).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal follow-up of heart failure patients after hospital discharge for acute cardiac decompensation (ACD) with predischarge LVEF <=40%, undergoing ongoing optimization of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), assessed over 6, 12, and 18 months.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A useful surrogate marker of cardiac remodeling and its reversal. Greater LVEF improvement at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) correlates with lower mortality risk and fewer all-cause or heart failure-related hospitalizations at 18 months. Its trajectory indicates myocardial capacity for repair. Worsening LVEF is a surrogate for attenuation/reversal of reverse remodeling and is associated with clinical worsening, particularly rehospitalization. Normalization of LVEF may not indicate true disease recovery, highlighting the need for ongoing therapy.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated levels were observed in the context of persistent hemodynamic congestion and residual heart failure signs/symptoms at 6-month follow-up (FUP6). No specific quantification was provided, but these levels predict risk.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Involved in vasodilation, fluid balance, and inflammation; it serves as a marker of hemodynamic stress and systemic congestion.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Persistent hemodynamic congestion and residual heart failure signs and symptoms in patients from all heart failure categories at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels predict the risk of rehospitalization across all heart failure subgroups, suggesting ongoing hemodynamic stress.
